cues.en: If I showed you this paint chip and asked you to tell me what color it is, what would you say?
cues.zh: 如果我给你看这块色卡，问你它是什么颜色，你会怎么说？

cues.en: How about this one and this one? You probably said blue, purple and brown, but if your native language is Wobey from Cote D'Ivoire, you probably would have used one word for all three.
cues.zh: 那这块和这块呢？你可能会说蓝色、紫色和棕色，但如果你的母语是科特迪瓦的Wobey语，你可能三个都用同一个词。

cues.en: That's because not all languages have the same number of basic color categories.
cues.zh: 这是因为并非所有语言的基本颜色类别数量都相同。

cues.en: In English, we have 11. Russian has 12, But some languages like Wobe only have three. And researchers have found that if a language only has three or four basic colors, they can usually predict what those will be.
cues.zh: 英语有11种，俄语有12种，但像Wobe这样的语言只有3种。研究人员发现，如果一种语言只有三四种基本颜色，通常能预测出是哪些。

cues.en: So how do they do it?
cues.zh: 那他们是怎么做到的呢？

cues.en: As you would expect, different languages have different words for colors.
cues.zh: 正如你所料，不同语言对颜色有不同的词。

cues.en: But what interests researchers isn't those simple translations. It's the question of which colors get names at all.
cues.zh: 但研究者感兴趣的不是那些简单的翻译，而是哪些颜色会被命名的问题。

cues.en: Because as much as we think of colors in categories,
cues.zh: 因为尽管我们把颜色按类别来想，

cues.en: the truth is that color is a spectrum. It's not obvious why we should have a basic color term for this color, but not this one. And until the nineteen sixties, it was widely believed by anthropologists that cultures would just choose from the spectrum randomly.
cues.zh: 事实是颜色是一个连续谱。为什么这个颜色应该有一个基本颜色词，而那个却没有，这并不显而易见。直到20世纪60年代，人类学家普遍认为各文化会从光谱中随机选择。

cues.en: But in 1969,
two Berkeley researchers Paul K and Brent Berlin published a book challenging that assumption. They had asked 20 people who spoke different languages to look at these 330
cues.zh: 两位伯克利的研究者Paul K和Brent Berlin出版了一本书，挑战了这一假设。他们让20位讲不同语言的人看这330

cues.en: color chips and categorized each of them by their basic color term. And they found hints of a universal pattern. If a language had six basic color words, they were always for black or dark, white or light, red, green, yellow, and blue. If it had four terms, were for black, white, red, and then either green or yellow. If it had only three, they were always for black, white, and red.
cues.zh: 张色卡，并按各自语言的基本颜色词对每张进行分类。结果他们发现了普遍模式的线索。如果一种语言有六个基本颜色词，那总是对应黑或暗、白或亮、红、绿、黄、蓝。如果有四个词，则是黑、白、红，再加绿或黄之一。如果只有三个词，那总是黑、白、红。

cues.en: It suggested that as languages develop, they create color names in a certain order. First black and white, then red, then green and yellow, then blue, then others like brown, purple, pink, orange, and gray.
cues.zh: 有研究提出，语言在发展过程中，会按特定顺序创造颜色名称。先是黑和白，然后是红，接着是绿和黄，再是蓝，之后才是棕、紫、粉、橙和灰等颜色。

cues.en: The theory was revolutionary.
cues.zh: 这个理论是革命性的。

cues.en: They weren't the first researchers interested in the question of how we name colors.
cues.zh: 他们并不是最早研究颜色命名问题的研究者。

cues.en: William Glad stone, who would later become a four term British prime minister, published a book on the ancient Greek works of Homer.
cues.zh: 威廉·格莱斯顿出版了一本关于荷马古希腊著作的书，他后来四次出任英国首相。

cues.en: He was struck by the fact that there weren't many colors at all in the text. And when there were, Homer would use the same word for, quote, colors which, according to us, are essentially different. He used the same word for purple to describe blood, a dark cloud, a wave, and a rainbow and he referred to the sea as wine looking.
cues.zh: 他注意到文本中根本没有多少颜色词。而当出现颜色时，Homer会用同一个词来指代那些在我们看来本质不同的颜色。他用同一个表示紫色的词来描述血、乌云、海浪和彩虹，还把大海称为“酒色的”。

cues.en: Gladstone didn't find any references to blue or orange at all.
cues.zh: Gladstone完全找不到任何对蓝色或橙色的指称。

cues.en: Some researchers took this and other ancient writings to wrongly speculate that earlier societies were color blind.
cues.zh: 一些研究者据此和其他古代文献，错误地推测早期社会是色盲的。

cues.en: Later in the nineteenth century, an anthropologist named W. H. R. Rivers went on an expedition to Papua New Guinea where he found that some tribes only had words for red, white, and black,
cues.zh: 十九世纪后期，一位名叫 W. H. R. Rivers 的人类学家前往巴布亚新几内亚考察，他发现有些部落只有红、白、黑三个词，

cues.en: while others had additional words for blue and green.
cues.zh: 而另一些部落还有蓝和绿的额外词汇。

cues.en: An expedition to investigate the cultures on a remote group of islands in the Torres Straits between Australia and New Guinea. His brief was to investigate the mental characteristics
cues.zh: 一次考察，目的是调查澳大利亚与巴布亚新几内亚之间托雷斯海峡偏远群岛上的文化。他的任务是研究这些岛民的

cues.en: of the islanders.
cues.zh: 心理特征。

cues.en: He claims that the number of color terms in a population was related to their, quote, intellectual and cultural development.
cues.zh: 他声称，一个群体中颜色词的数量与其所谓的智力和文化发展水平有关。

cues.en: And he used his findings to claim that Papuans were less physically evolved than Europeans.
cues.zh: 他用他的发现来声称巴布亚人在生理上不如欧洲人进化得好。

cues.en: Berlin and Kay didn't make those racist claims, but their color hierarchy attracted a lot of criticism.
cues.zh: Berlin和Kay没有提出那些种族主义主张，但他们的颜色等级制度招致了很多批评。

cues.en: For one thing, critics pointed out that the study used a small sample size. 20 people, all of whom were bilingual English speakers, not monolingual native speakers. And almost all of the languages were from industrialized societies,
cues.zh: 一方面，批评者指出这项研究的样本量很小。20个人，全都是会说英语的双语者，而不是单语母语者。而且几乎所有的语言都来自工业化社会，

cues.en: hardly the best portrait of the entire world. But it also had to do with defining what a basic color term is.
cues.zh: 很难说是对整个世界的最佳描绘。但这也与如何定义基本颜色词有关。

cues.en: In the Yalay language in Papua New Guinea, for example, there are only basic color terms for black, white, and red. But there's a broad vocabulary of everyday objects like the sky, ashes, and tree sap that are used as color comparisons that cover almost all English color words.
cues.zh: 比如，在巴布亚新几内亚的Yalay语中，只有黑、白、红这三种基本颜色词。但日常物品的词汇很丰富，比如天空、灰烬、树液，它们被用来作颜色对比，几乎涵盖了所有英语颜色词。

cues.en: There are also languages like Hanuno'o
cues.zh: 也有像Hanuno'o这样的语言

cues.en: from The Philippines where a word can communicate both color and a physical feeling. They have four basic terms to describe color, but they're on a spectrum of light versus dark, strength versus weakness, and wetness versus dryness.
cues.zh: 来自菲律宾，一个词可以同时传达颜色和身体感觉。他们有四个描述颜色的基本词，但它们处于光明与黑暗、强与弱、湿与干的谱系上。

cues.en: Those kinds of languages don't fit neatly into a color chip
cues.zh: 这类语言没法整齐地归入某个色块

cues.en: test.
cues.zh: 测试。

cues.en: But by the late nineteen seventies, Berlin and Kay had a response for the critics.
cues.zh: 但到了20世纪70年代末，Berlin和Kay对批评者做出了回应。

cues.en: They called it the world color survey. They conducted the same labeling test on over 2,600 native speakers of a 110 unwritten languages from non industrialized societies.
cues.zh: 他们称之为世界颜色调查。他们对来自非工业化社会的110种无文字语言的2600多名母语者进行了相同的标记测试。

cues.en: They found that with some tweaks, the color hierarchy still checked out. 83% of the languages fit into the hierarchy.
cues.zh: 他们发现，经过一些调整，颜色层级依然成立。83%的语言符合这一层级。

cues.en: And when they averaged the center point of where each speaker labeled each of their language's colors, they wound up with a sort of heat map. Those clusters matched pretty closely to the English speakers' averages, which are labeled here. Here's how Paul K puts it. It it just turns out that most languages make cuts in the same place.
cues.zh: 当他们把每位说话者为各自语言中每种颜色标注的中心点取平均时，得到了一张类似热力图的东西。这些聚类与英语说话者的平均值相当吻合，图中已标出。Paul K 是这样说的：结果就是，大多数语言都在相同的位置做了切分。

cues.en: Some languages
cues.zh: 有些语言

cues.en: make fewer cuts than others.
cues.zh: 做的切分比别的语言少。

cues.en: So these color stages are widespread throughout the world.
cues.zh: 所以这些颜色阶段在世界各地普遍存在。

cues.en: But why? Why would a word for red come before a word for blue? Some have speculated that the sages correspond to the salience of the color and the natural environment.
cues.zh: 但为什么呢？为什么表示红色的词会比表示蓝色的词更早出现？有人推测，这与圣贤对颜色和自然环境中显著性的认知有关。

cues.en: Red is in blood and in dirt. Blue, on the other hand, was fairly scarce before manufacturing.
cues.zh: 红色存在于血液和泥土中。而蓝色在制造业出现之前相当稀少。

cues.en: Recently, cognitive science researchers have explored this question by running computer simulations of how language evolves through conversations
cues.zh: 最近，认知科学研究者通过计算机模拟语言如何在人与人的对话中演变，来探讨这个问题。

cues.en: between people. The simulations presented artificial agents with multiple colors at a time. And through a series of simple negotiations,
cues.zh: 模拟中，人工代理会同时看到多种颜色。经过一系列简单的协商，

cues.en: those agents developed shared labels for the different colors.
cues.zh: 这些代理为不同颜色发展出了共享的标签。

cues.en: And the order in which those labels emerged?
cues.zh: 那些标签出现的顺序是怎样的？

cues.en: First, reddish tones, then green and yellow,
cues.zh: 首先是红色调，然后是绿色和黄色，

cues.en: then blue, then orange.
cues.zh: 然后是蓝色，然后是橙色。

cues.en: It matched the original stages pretty closely.
cues.zh: 它与最初的几个阶段相当吻合。

cues.en: And it suggests that there's something about the colors themselves that leads to this hierarchy.
cues.zh: 这表明颜色本身存在某种特性，导致了这种层级关系。

cues.en: Red is fundamentally more distinct than the other colors.
cues.zh: 红色从根本上比其他颜色更具区分度。

cues.en: So what does all this mean? Why does it matter? Well, it tells us that despite our many differences across cultures and societies,
cues.zh: 那么这一切意味着什么？为什么重要？它告诉我们，尽管不同文化和社会之间存在诸多差异，

cues.en: there is something universal about how humans try to make sense of the world.
cues.zh: 人类在理解世界的方式上存在着某种共通之处。
